text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- After a marathon session of Austria's government coalition partners, the Social Democrats and Conservatives agreed to sell the government's 70 percent voting stake in Creditanstalt to Bank Austria.

Bank Austria will pay 17.16 billion schillings for the country's second largest bank. Creditanstalt will remain independent for at least five years. Small shareholders will be offered to swap their shares or sell them.
The City of Vienna will reduce its holding in Bank Austria to under 20 percent in the next seven years.
The government has said future privatisations should only go hand in hand with the coalition partner, so as not to threaten the relationship of the two parties.
Bank Austria chief executive Gerhard Randa expects earnings per share to double over the next five years.
- Chrysler will create 700 additional jobs at its Eurostar plant in southern Austria by introducing a third shift. Capacity should be improved to 78,000 cars per year from 50,000.
- Conservative People's Party sees security policies as the next possible stumbling block for the coalition.
- Social Democrats see the sale of Creditanstalt to Bank Austria as a success while the People's Party see it as a bearable compromise.

- Social Democrats and People's Party have agreed to work together on a new privatisation law as conservative chief whip Andreas Khol has said his party would not go it alone with the far-right Freedom Party.
DIE PRESSE
- Even though the coalition was saved by the last-minute agreement on the sale of Creditanstalt, mistrust remains. Bank Austria will sell GiroCredit for Creditanstalt.
- The sale of Creditanstalt ended as a full success for Bank Austria, while a few of the People's Party's demands were met.
- The Bank Austria/Creditanstalt merger will shake up Austria's banking sector. The coalition parties agreed on making new laws on privatisation and the capital market.
KURIER
- After the sale of Creditanstalt everyone feels a winner -- the coalition government could be saved in the last minute.
- Raiffeisen bank wants to take over Creditanstalt's three regional banks, Oberbank, Bank fuer Kaernten und Steiermark and Bank fuer Tirol und Vorarlberg.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- Since Creditanstalt has been sold to Bank Austria, peace within Austria's coalition will be kept until Tuesday, when a special session of parliament is scheduled.
- The new banking group made up of Creditanstalt and Bank Austria plans to double profits. Bank Austria plans to pay for the takeover with its own cash.
Creditanstalt's cooperation with insurer EA-Generali and building society Wuestenrot, both members of the consortium which planned to take over Creditanstalt too, should remain intact.
- The international consortium headed by EA-Generali regrets it failed in its bid to buy Creditanstalt.
KRONEN ZEITUNG
- The winners in the Creditanstalt privatisation are Finance Minister Viktor Klima and the taxpayer.
